newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Saurer says profit up in first four months.
newsitem.headline: Saurer says profit up in first four months.

text.p: Swiss industrial conglomerate Saurer AG said that its group profits rose to 16 million Swiss francs in January to April 1997, compared with from 2.0 million the comparable 1996 period.
It also said its turnover in the same period rose to 557 million Swiss francs from 530 million.
It said orders in hand rose to 648 million from 440 million.
The company manufactuers textile machinery and automobile components.
It said that it expected the rest of 1997 to continue the positive trend.
"In view of the level of orders on hand and of the delivery plans, we expect the profits to develop positively for the remainder of 1997," Saurer said in a statement.
It also expected further positive impact from introduction into the market of new products, especially with respect to winding and ring spinning systems, Saurer said.

It said group operating profit also rose to 23 million Swiss francs from five million. It said a recent restructuring had improved cost structures, and other changes tied to the restructuring, "are beginning to have an increasing effect".
It said both Schlafhorst and Zinser units had shown substantial improvements for the first few months, despite lower level of sales.
Non-textile companies Graziano Trasmissioni and Berna also showed very encouraging developments, Saurer said.
It also said acquisition of BB Industrie Holding was going ahead and would be concluded soon.
It said the extraordinary financial income arising from the BBI transaction was not yet fully reflected in results.
